body.statement:
Let \(q_{ni}\in\mathbb R^p\), where \(p\) is fixed, be a deterministic triangular array satisfying \(\sum_{i=1}^n q_{ni}=0\), \((n-1)^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^nq_{ni}q_{ni}^{\mathsf T}\to\Sigma\), and \(n^{-1}\max_{i\le n}\|q_{ni}\|^2\to0\).  If \(W_{n,0}\) is uniform on the balanced allocation space, then
\[
 n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^n(2W_{n,0,i}-1)q_{ni}\Rightarrow\mathcal N_p(0,\Sigma).
\]

source.locator: Theorem 5, specialized to two equal-sized treatment groups and a fixed-dimensional vector outcome
source.verbatim_statement: Under the setting of Theorem 3, if for any 1 <= q != r <= Q, S_q^2 and S_qr have limiting values, n_q/N has positive limiting value, and max_{1 <= q <= Q} max_{1 <= i <= N} ||Y_i(q) - bar Y(q)||_2^2/N -> 0, then N Var{hat tau(A)} has a limiting value, denoted by V, and sqrt(N){hat tau(A) - tau(A)} converges to N(0,V).

attestation.note: Verified from the authors arXiv source arXiv:1610.04821v1, FPCLT_1016_arxiv.tex, theorem labeled cor:fclt_exp_stable (Theorem 5 in the rendered paper). Specialize Q=2 with n_1=n_0=N/2, take the same centered fixed p-vector q_Ni as both potential-outcome vectors, and use contrast matrices A_1=I and A_0=-I. Since sum_i q_Ni=0, the estimator scaling gives N^(-1/2) sum_i (2W_i-1)q_Ni; its limiting covariance is Sigma. The node assumptions imply the theorem maximum condition and covariance limits.
